title: NY Fed's Williams Warns AI Chip Shortage Could Drag On Past Two Years
key_facts: New York Fed president John Williams told Bloomberg News on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026 that the AI chip supply crunch is unlikely to ease within two years.
He described a "pretty abrupt and large increase" in the cost of chips and goods that depend on them.
He said "I think it's going to take longer" when asked about balance within 24 months.
He still sees one more rate hike this year as possibly appropriate, which would lift the range to 4% to 4.25%.
He called many AI backers "relatively price insensitive".
High chip prices create incentives to build factories, but that takes considerable time.
quote_evidence: Asked directly whether supply and demand for AI equipment would come into balance over a 24-month horizon, Williams was blunt: "I think it's going to take longer."
"I haven't changed my view that it may be appropriate to have one more rate hike," he said.
why_it_matters_hint: A Fed voter says AI hardware shortages feed inflation and are not easily cooled by interest rates.
notes: Relayed by BigGo Finance from a Bloomberg interview; the interview was before 14 Oct 2026.
